source.title: Mixed Precision Training With 8-bit Floating Point
source.authors: Naveen Mellempudi; S. Srinivasan; Dipankar Das; Bharat Kaul

record.tranche_reason: Tests how reduced-precision training and rounding choices affect validation performance and overfitting in additional model and dataset settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on quantization noise, rounding, regularization, and validation performance. It does not test random-label memorization, width scaling, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, optimizer comparisons, batch-size effects, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. Figure 4a compares dropout and no explicit regularization, but the text gives no separate values for either condition.
record.test_reason: Section 3.2 and Figure 4a compare dropout with no explicit regularization in FP8 ResNet-50 training, testing V6 in a new numerical-precision setting. However, the supplied text reports only that both conditions outperform RNE with L2 regularization; it does not establish whether dropout improves on no explicit regularization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: enhanced loss scaling and stochastic rounding address underflow and quantization-noise problems in FP8 training, allowing performance broadly comparable to FP32. Their slight-improvement claim needs qualification: ResNet-18 and ResNet-50 improve, ResNet-34 is essentially unchanged, GNMT improves slightly, and Transformer BLEU falls from 23.6 to 23.0.
record.recipe_differences: Uses FP8 mixed-precision training and studies rounding and regularization effects; it does not use the original methods underlying the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Rounding method and explicit regularization affect the reported convergence and validation behavior; loss scaling also changes convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: FP8 ResNet-50 with RNE and L2 regularization has increased validation error while training error mostly follows the FP32 baseline. Both dropout and no explicit regularization perform better than this L2 condition. Stochastic rounding with L2 restores validation behavior close to full precision.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Rounding and regularization choices affect generalization during FP8 ResNet-50 training.

record.problems: The relevant comparisons are described mainly through figures; the text supplies no separate numeric validation values for the dropout and no-regularization conditions. The authors describe the source of the RNE overfitting as based on multiple experiments but do not provide their details here.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The paper's relevant rounding and quantization results do not measure a mapped version's named behavior closely enough to include as version rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to fit training data.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and tuning dependence.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover accuracy.
Very small training sets, excessive dropout, and removal of dropout together with weight decay under data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: The dropout-versus-no-explicit-regularization validation comparison needs a result row. The supplied figure caption establishes the comparison, but neither plotted values nor a textual statement of its direction are available. The shared improvement over L2 cannot establish dropout's benefit over no dropout.

record.verdict_notes: No existing rows require correction. V6 is tested by the experimental comparison, but its outcome cannot be determined from the supplied text, so no directional verdict is justified. The missing comparison is identified in the record's commentary but is not declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width scaling beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
The text does not state separate dropout-versus-no-dropout validation values or establish that dropout itself lowers test error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
